📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s representative to the Sixth Committee of the UN General Assembly has strongly condemned US-Israeli crimes against the peoples of Iran and Palestine, saying Israel must be held accountable for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity, and terrorist acts.

Speaking at the committee’s session in New York, the Iranian representative rejected allegations raised by the Israeli representative and said that Israel has sought since 2023 to divert attention from its actions against Palestinians and other countries in the region by making “baseless allegations” against others.
​
He said the international community’s inaction has allowed the scope of Israeli crimes to expand year after year.
​
Responding to Israeli remarks concerning the events of October 7, he said that from October 7, 2023, to October 7, 2026, an average of at least 70 to 75 people have been killed every day in the region by Israel.
​
He added that more than 75,000 Palestinians, as well as thousands of people in Iran and other countries in the region, have been killed during the period.
​
The Iranian representative also pointed to the killing of an average of 28 children every day in Gaza, saying the figure was equivalent to losing a classroom every day and demonstrated the scale of the killing of children.
​
Referring to Israeli attacks on Iranian families, he said 16 members of one family were killed in one attack merely because one of the family members was a university professor.
​
He described Israel as a serious threat to international peace and security, saying the term “child-killing regime” was an accurate description of Israel and that its officials could not evade responsibility for their crimes by making accusations against others.
​
Iran rejects US claims on civilian protection
​
The Iranian representative also responded to a claim by the US representative concerning Washington’s commitment to protecting civilians, citing the February 28 attack on Shajareh Tayyebeh primary school in Minab, southern Iran.
​
He said 168 children and teachers were killed in the attack, noting that the victims were between seven and 12 years old.
​
“They were learning, playing and waiting to return to the arms of their families. That was not a battlefield, but a primary school. They were not military personnel; they were just children,” he said.
​
The Iranian representative also called for an end to impunity for perpetrators of such crimes in accordance with international law.

Baba Anya stepped out, spotting elderly men playing dominoes. *“Too old, too bearded, too short… Ah, this one’s just right!”* she thought, calling out: — Young man!  
— Me? — he asked, surprised.  
— Yes, you! Join me for a meal. Eating alone is dull.  
— I’d love to — but I’m a connoisseur. No simple borscht. I expect dessert.  
— You nearly offended me! Forgive you? Only with flowers.  
— Wildflowers? I saw some behind the building.  
Just then, 12-year-old Nastya skipped over: — Grandma! Grandpa! On a date?  
Baba Anya huffed: — Tsk, Nastya, you ruined it! Home early? Come, soup’s ready.  
To the man: — Go on, old stump. I only came to call you for lunch.  
Walking inside, she muttered: *Hmph. Dessert, indeed…*

The breach highlights a persistent vulnerability in crypto: while blockchain transactions can be pseudonymous, KYC and compliance records held by centralized services create a paper trail that, if exposed, can permanently de-anonymize users.

Bohol's Chocolate Hills, Philippines

The Chocolate Hills of Bohol are one of the Philippines’ most iconic natural attractions—famous for their surreal landscape of over 1,200 perfectly cone-shaped mounds that turn a rich chocolate brown during the dry season.

Spread across approximately 19 square miles in the towns of Carmen, Batuan, and Sagbayan, this geological marvel is recognized as the country’s third National Geological Monument. Often hailed as the Eighth Wonder of the World, the hills are so emblematic they’re even printed on the Philippine 200-peso bill.

Though Bohol is smaller than nearby islands like Cebu, it packs a powerful punch when it comes to beauty and adventure. At the heart of it all are the Chocolate Hills tours—thoughtfully curated experiences that make it easy to explore the breathtaking viewpoints and uncover the fascinating science behind this phenomenon.
